hook: The Jewish girl whose diary, written in hiding from the Nazis, is read all over the world.

pages.x: Anne Frank was born in Frankfurt in 1929. When the Nazis came to power, her Jewish family moved to Amsterdam, where her father, Otto, ran a small business.
For her 13th birthday, in June 1942, she was given a red and white checked diary. She wrote in it as if to a friend, whom she called Kitty.

In July 1942, when her sister Margot was ordered to report to a labour camp, the family went into hiding in rooms behind a bookcase in her father's office building. Eight people hid there for two years, fed by his loyal staff.

By day they had to keep silent while workers moved about below. Anne pinned pictures of film stars on her wall, quarrelled with her mother, fell in love with a boy named Peter, and gazed at a chestnut tree from the attic.
In 1944 she heard on the radio that diaries would be collected after the war, and began rewriting hers as a book. She dreamed of becoming a writer.
On 4 August 1944 the police raided the annex, probably after a tip-off. Who betrayed them is still not known. All eight were sent to Auschwitz.
Anne and Margot were moved to the camp at Bergen-Belsen, where both died of typhus early in 1945, weeks before it was freed. Anne was 15. Of the eight, only her father survived.
One of their helpers, Miep Gies, had saved the diary. Otto published it in 1947. It has been translated into more than 70 languages and read by tens of millions of people.

pages.x: Anne Frank's diary gives a face and a voice to the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust. Her hiding place is now a museum visited by more than a million people a year.

A voice for the victims of the Holocaust
